description: The item contract for the shared OBSERVATORY_METRICS DynamoDB table, provisioned by
the tarun-teamweave-shared stack and written by every weave service that emits span
telemetry. The table has many writers in different languages and several readers that
build dashboards from it, none of which can see each other's code, so the item shape
is a cross-repository interface and is pinned here rather than in any one consumer.
Copies vendored into consumer repositories must carry the same version string; a
conformance test in each repository asserts its writer or reader against this file.

note: DynamoDB attribute names are case sensitive and the table declares these exactly.
An item whose key attributes are spelled any other way (PK/SK, Pk/Sk) is rejected
by PutItem with a ValidationException, which a writer that swallows exceptions
will report as success while writing nothing at all.

sk_grammar.rationale: Readers range-query on sk lexicographically, so the timestamp must sort first and must be UTC ISO 8601.

note: The namespace is what makes a row findable. A reader queries whole partitions by
exact pk, so a writer using a namespace no reader enumerates is writing rows that
are durable, billable and permanently invisible to every dashboard.
This is the namespace the shared library exporter writes. No reader queries it.
Migrating a service off its vendored copy onto the library exporter (the stated
point of platform edge E2) therefore removes that service from every dashboard
without any error surfacing. Resolving this is a platform decision recorded in
docs/integration-audit.md, not something a consumer repository can fix alone.

recommended_attributes.service: S -- the emitting service; the only attribute that identifies a row's origin once several writers share a namespace

invariants: I1: key attributes are spelled 'pk' and 'sk' in lower case
I2: pk matches {namespace}#{discriminator} with a namespace listed in namespace_registry
I4: ttl is present and is a Unix epoch in the future, so rows expire rather than accumulate
I5: a writer's namespace has at least one reader, or is explicitly marked status=unread here
